title: Maximal-Ratio LLR Diversity Combining vs. Unweighted Majority Voting Across Heterogeneous Branches
claims: Across L heterogeneous CNOT branches with visibilities gamma_1, ..., gamma_L, the exact Bayesian posterior LLR is sum_{l=1}^L 2 * atanh(gamma_l) * y_l.

When a high-visibility branch is combined with noisy branches, unweighted majority voting can degrade error >3.2x below single-best selection, whereas LLR combining strictly dominates both unweighted majority and single-best selection.
